correctness.rationale: The source bounds every normalized difference by P(a,x) with a>=1 and x=2rho/(1-rho)>0 and proves sup P=C0. On a>1,x>0 it proves no critical point; at a=1 the inward derivative is positive, so no finite-domain point can realize the global supremum. This gives strictness for every distinct pair. For an extremizing sequence, the source's uniform large-a decay and large-x bound keep parameters in bounded ranges. If x failed to tend to zero, compactness would produce a finite maximizer, contradicting strictness. Uniform convergence P(a,x)->B(a)=2a(a-1)e^{1-a} on bounded a-ranges then gives B(a_j)->C0; B has the unique maximizer a0=(3+sqrt(5))/2, hence a_j->a0. The transformations recover rho_j->0 and alpha_j=a_j e^{1-a_j}->a0 e^{1-a0}. No finite numerical experiment is used.

final_claim: The sharp pseudo-hyperbolic Bloch constant C0 for nonconstant locally univalent harmonic Bloch mappings is never attained by distinct points; every normalized extremizing sequence has pseudo-hyperbolic separation tending to zero and its larger endpoint Bloch level tending to ((3+sqrt(5))/2) exp(-(1+sqrt(5))/2).
scientific_limitations: An equivalent extremizing-sequence observation could exist under extremal-function terminology outside the targeted Bloch literature.
The rigidity is only for the scalar proof parameters; it does not prove convergence of the harmonic mappings themselves after normalization.
